owner: NEREID cascade and shared GCC 13 build compatibility

implementation.note: Direct map-slot construction and named camera JSON lifetime remove the original GCC warning without changing accepted values; later diagnostics are addressed in the same branch.

architecture.note: Existing NEREID, game ECS and policy-test owners are reused; the repair adds no solver or game-specific engine layer.

native_api.note: Existing native cascade and Combat APIs retain their signatures; focused NEREID and game regression tests exercise them.

skill.note: Compiler compatibility repair introduces no authoring operation or user-facing skill surface.

mcp.note: No new editor or MCP operation is introduced by the compiler repair.

studio.note: No new Studio control or behavior is introduced.

inspector.note: No inspected data shape or UI is changed.

persistence.note: Cascade and Combat serialization formats remain unchanged.

graphs.note: No graph nodes, assets or execution semantics are changed.

performance.note: The Mac NEREID review fixture exercises cascade insertion, replacement and duplicate rejection. The complete fixture used 0.25 s user CPU and 8,511,488 bytes peak RSS in one run.

platforms.note: Verified the affected Combat and Vulkan translation units with GCC 13.5 on Linux arm64 and the NEREID and policy fixtures on macOS. Full hosted Linux CI was cancelled.

dependencies.note: No dependency, package or build configuration was added.

headless.note: This change does not add a simulation operation; existing native headless tests remain in the Mac quick gate.

examples.note: No new API or data format requires an example.

tests.note: The two focused Mac tests passed for cascade ownership and policy fixtures.

handoff.note: Per-stage commits, SHAs, failures and next actions are recorded in the owner handoff.

documentation.note: The NEREID roadmap item and repair handoff describe the bounded compiler fix and verification state.

publishing.note: The repair has no new visible output or web demo; the prior camera feature retains its published evidence.
